newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher led by Teva.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher led by Teva.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Tuesday, led by a sharp rise in Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.27 percent, or 2.65 points, to 211.04 on all-share turnover of 92 million shekels against 57 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 1.18 percent to 219.11.
On Monday there was no trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange due to a general strike by the Histadrut trade union federation.

Trading will be suspended on Wednesday to enable the exchange to change its system for valuing share prices. From January 2, trading will be conducted in "whole" share prices as opposed to the current system of trading in percentages of shares' par value.
The change is technical and will not alter the actual value of the shares.
"Teva led the market today and the whole market followed it," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities and Investments.
Teva led the most actives and surged 5.5 percent to 162,488 on volume of 10.2 million shekels. On Monday, its Nasdaq-traded share rose 5.8 percent to an all-time high of $50.3.
Last week Teva won U.S. marketing approval for its Copaxone multiple sclerosis treatment.

"The rise of Israeli shares traded on Nasdaq had a strong impact on trading today. The session opened with nice gains of 1.5 percent, but towards the end of the day investors started taking profits," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.
"Today's rise was the market's finale for the year. Options reflect expectations for further profit-taking on Thursday, but the positive trend is expected to continue in January," the trader said.

"December was a very good month for the market and we hope the positive trend continues in January. Stocks are very cheap and inflation is expected to decline in 1997," Finn said. "I believe the positive momentum will continue."

Supersol Ltd gained 0.75 percent to 7,944. In a report released in Israel on Tuesday, Lehman Brothers assigned Supersol a 1-buy rating and set a target price for the end of 1997 of 94 shekels a share.
Elbit surged 5.25 percent to 2,328, which traders attributed to a technical correction.

Israel Land Development Co, the second most active share, rose the maximum 10 percent to 1,189 on turnover of 5.7 million shekels after the company said it would pay an annual dividend. Traders said Bank Hapoalim was the main buyer.
FIBI Holdings, the number three most active, gained 1.0 percent to 46,489. Traders said there was no evident reason for the activity in the share.
